subtitle: Digital Sustainability Companion
paragraphs: The Digital Sustainability Companion is a research project at LUT University. We are developing a desktop application for employees who use a computer in their daily work. The aim is to help them understand selected digital activities and consider changes to their habits.

The application will monitor idle time, running applications, available power-management information and local storage use. These indicators will inform Energy Efficiency and Storage Efficiency sub-scores, which will be combined into an overall Digital Sustainability Score (DSS). The application will also generate rule-based recommendations. Monitoring, scoring and core recommendations are designed to run locally, including when the computer is offline.

Users will be able to review their scores over time, receive practical suggestions and choose which activities to monitor. For example, someone whose computer is often left idle might receive a suggestion to review their sleep settings.

metadata.title: Project | Digital Sustainability Companion
metadata.description: The proposed Digital Sustainability Companion: local monitoring, indicator-based scoring, recommendations and a planned user evaluation at LUT University.

research.introduction: We are developing a desktop application to help LUT University employees understand selected computer activities and consider more sustainable digital habits.
research.methodDescription: We will build the companion and test it with LUT University employees. Their feedback will help us understand how useful it is, how easy it is to use and whether it helps them make changes to their everyday computer habits.

architecture.title: How the companion will work
architecture.introduction: Select a component to read its role in the proposed system. The diagram shows planned connections, not live data transfers.
architecture.localDescription: The companion will help users review their computer use, see their scores and get practical suggestions, even without an internet connection.
architecture.cloudDescription: External communication will require user consent. Research sharing will use approved, anonymized or aggregated summaries; AI requests will contain only the information needed for an explanation.
architecture.storageConnection: Solid: Internal application and backend communication.
architecture.cloudConnection: Dotted: Optional external communication or consent-dependent data transmission.

monitoring.title: Activity monitoring
monitoring.summary: Idle time, applications, power and storage
monitoring.description: The monitoring module will collect selected activity information at configurable intervals. Users will be able to enable, disable or configure supported monitoring functions.
items: Idle time, running applications and available power-management information
Local storage usage, with relevant monitoring records saved in SQLite
Optional access to supported cloud storage providers, with explicit permission

analysis.title: Sustainability analysis
analysis.description: The analytics engine will validate monitoring information, calculate Energy Efficiency and Storage Efficiency sub-scores and combine them into an overall DSS.
items: Energy Efficiency and Storage Efficiency
Scores stored locally and made available to the interface and recommendation engine
DSS is an indicator-based score, not a direct measurement of electricity consumption or carbon emissions

recommendations.title: Recommendation engine
recommendations.description: Local rules will use monitoring indicators and scores to generate recommendations and basic notifications. Generated recommendations will be stored in SQLite. Optional AI services may explain recommendations, but will not replace the local rule-based system.
items: Recommendations based on defined conditions, such as prolonged inactivity or power settings
Local storage of recommendations and user notification preferences
Optional AI explanations requested through the backend only when enabled

dashboard.title: User interface
dashboard.description: The interface will bring together your activity summaries, scores and recommendations. You will also be able to review saved results and change your monitoring and notification settings.
items: Initial interface: Dashboard, DSS, Recommendations and Settings
Basic notifications with user controls
Historical visualizations and weekly reports

storage.title: Local database (SQLite)
storage.description: Your activity information, settings, score history and recommendations will be saved on your computer, so you can review previous results even without an internet connection.
items: Monitoring records or aggregated measurements needed for scoring
User settings, DSS history and generated recommendations
Storage for periodic reports when reporting is implemented

cloud.title: Cloud backend
cloud.description: This online service will support optional AI explanations of users' recommendations and, with their permission, share a summary of their results for research. Users will still be able to use the companion's monitoring, scores and recommendations without an internet connection.
items: Optional AI explanations to help users understand their recommendations
Authorized, anonymized or aggregated research summaries stored in PostgreSQL
Local monitoring, scoring and rules remain available if backend services are unavailable

cloudStorage.title: Cloud storage providers
cloudStorage.description: The DSC may connect to cloud storage services, such as Google Drive or OneDrive, to collect information about users' storage usage with their permission. This feature is optional and may be added in future versions of the application.
items: Explicit user permission before access
Information about how much cloud storage users are using
Cloud storage usage shown alongside local storage usage

ai.title: AI explanation service
ai.description: The backend may use Azure OpenAI or the OpenAI API to provide explanations of locally generated recommendations.
items: Enabled only with user consent
Local recommendations remain available without AI

researchDatabase.title: Research database (PostgreSQL)
researchDatabase.description: The backend will save and retrieve approved, anonymized or appropriately aggregated research information in PostgreSQL.
items: Research sharing requires user authorization
No direct connection from the React interface to PostgreSQL
Separate from the local SQLite database

architecture.ipcConnection: Arrows at both ends show information moving in both directions, such as requesting saved results and receiving them for display.
architecture.externalDescription: With users' permission, the companion can also check your cloud storage use. Optional AI explanations and research data sharing use an online service.

evaluation.title: How the application will be evaluated
evaluation.introduction: Testing will check whether the application works as intended and how much computing resource it uses. User evaluation will examine usability, satisfaction and changes in digital habits.

items.title: Functionality and offline use
items.description: Test monitoring, score calculations, recommendation rules, notifications, local storage and behaviour when external services are unavailable.

items.title: Resource consumption
items.description: Measure CPU and memory use, startup time, monitoring overhead and disk activity.

items.title: Privacy and user control
items.description: Check local processing, controlled Electron interfaces, permission settings and the information included in authorized external requests.

items.title: Usability
items.description: Ask participants to complete typical tasks, use the System Usability Scale (SUS) and collect feedback on confusing or difficult parts of the interface.

items.title: User satisfaction
items.description: Collect feedback about the usefulness of scores, recommendations, notifications and reports when available.

items.title: Digital habits
items.description: Evaluate behavioural change separately from the DSS by comparing monitored digital activities and sustainability indicators before and after users receive DSC feedback and recommendations. Participant feedback and engagement with recommendations may also be considered.

contributions.title: What we expect to learn and produce

items.title: A desktop application for evaluation
items.description: An application that combines local monitoring, sustainability scoring and rule-based recommendations for use in the university workplace.

items.title: Evidence about sustainability feedback
items.description: Findings on how participants use the companion, whether their monitored habits change and which parts of the application they find useful or difficult.
